about:
# RangeShade

Shades action bar buttons red when your target is out of range. An addon for World of Warcraft: Forever (client 1.60.x).

**Flashes buttons when they're ready again:** when an ability comes off cooldown, its button gives two quick bright pulses, so you see it's ready without watching the swirl. In fights only by default (`/rangeshade flash` cycles: in fights, always, off). The short global cooldown never flashes. Pairs well with the game's own "Show Numbers for Cooldowns" (Options > Action Bars).

## What it does

When an ability cannot reach your target, World of Warcraft only turns the small keybind text on its button red. RangeShade tints the whole icon red, so it is obvious at a glance.

It covers the eight standard action bars. When a button is back in range it gets the game's normal colour back, including the blue out-of-mana tint and the grey unusable one.

## Options

Type `/rangeshade` (or `/rshade`) to open the options, or use the addon's entry in the minimap's addon list.

| Setting | What it does | Command |
|---|---|---|
| Shade out-of-range buttons red | Turns the addon on or off | `/rangeshade on`, `off`, `toggle` |
| Melee abilities too | Also shades melee attacks (see below) | `/rangeshade melee` |
| Shading | Strong or soft red | `/rangeshade strong`, `soft` |

## Melee abilities

On the Forever client the game reports melee abilities as "in range" however far away the target is, so RangeShade measures the distance for those itself. The shortest distance the game will measure for an addon is about 10 yards, so a melee button clears a little before you are actually close enough to hit.

## Known limits

- The pet bar and stance bar are not covered.
- During combat the game restricts what addons may read. Where it will not report range, a button is left unshaded.
- `/rangeshade debug` lists what the game reports for each button, which helps explain why one is or is not shaded.

## Controller

With a game controller, the **B** button closes the RangeShade options, like the X and Escape do. While a window is open, B closes it; once it is closed, B goes back to whatever you have it set to. When a fight starts, B goes straight back to its usual job, even with the window open.

## More from this author

Other small addons for World of Warcraft: Forever, all free:

- **[GatherLog](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/gatherlog)** remembers ore, herbs, fishing pools, skinning spots, chests and rares across all your characters, and guides you back to the best spots.
- **[MouseTip](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/mousetip)** shows tooltips at your mouse cursor.
- **[JunkMate](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/junkmate)** sells junk and repairs at vendors, makes room for loot when your bags are full, and tidies your bank.
- **[AltGlance](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/altglance)** shows all your characters at a glance: level, gold, rested and where you left them.
- **[SwiftQuest](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/swiftquest)** accepts quests and hands them in as soon as you talk to the quest giver, without ever choosing a reward for you.
- **[SessionRecap](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/sessionrecap)** keeps a running tally of your play session: gold, experience per hour, quests, gathering and loot.
- **[MacroKit](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/macrokit)** adds ready-made macros for your class and spec, for all nine classes, and never overwrites your own.
- **[ZoomPad](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/zoompad)** puts big + and - buttons on screen that zoom the camera, made for the Steam Deck touchscreen.
- **[GamepadMacros](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/gamepadmacros)** adds ready-made macros for controller and Steam Deck players: heal yourself, use a quest item, save and wear gear, leave a group, emotes.
- **[FDR - Flight Data Recorder](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/fdr-flight-data-recorder)** times every flight-master flight and counts your next one down to landing.

## Installing

Copy this folder into `World of Warcraft\_forever_\Interface\AddOns\` as `RangeShade`, restart the game, and enable RangeShade on the character select screen.

## Developing

- `tools\Link-Addon.ps1` links this folder into the game's AddOns folder, so edits are live after `/reload`.
- `python tests/run.py` runs the tests (`pip install lupa` once). They run the addon in real Lua 5.1 against a fake of the game's API.
- `tools\Publish.ps1 -Message "..."` runs the tests and pushes to GitHub. GitHub runs the tests again on every push.

## Releasing

`tools\Publish.ps1 -Message "Release x.y.z" -Tag vx.y.z` publishes and tags. The tag makes GitHub package the addon and attach the zip to a GitHub release.

To also upload to CurseForge and Wago, two things are needed once:

1. Create the project on each site, then add its ID to `RangeShade.toc`:
   `## X-Curse-Project-ID: 123456` and `## X-Wago-ID: abc123`.
2. Create an upload token on each site and add it to this repository's secrets (Settings, Secrets and variables, Actions) as `CF_API_KEY` and `WAGO_API_TOKEN`.

Before each release: raise `## Version:` in `RangeShade.toc` and add the version to `CHANGELOG.md`.

# RangeShade

## 0.4.0

- **Melee shading no longer switches itself off for good.** Where the game won't let addons measure melee distance in a fight, melee buttons are now shaded only out of fights (one chat line says so); before, one refusal turned melee shading off for the whole session. Ranged buttons are shaded as usual.
- **Lighter on the game:** whether the target is beyond melee reach is worked out once per update instead of once per button, and which buttons hold melee attacks is remembered until your bars change. This matters more now that RangeShade watches the controller layout's buttons too.
- **Optional red border** around out-of-range buttons, easier to see on a small screen: in the options or `/rangeshade border`. Off by default.
- Listed in the game's own Options > AddOns. Key bindings to open the options and to switch shading on or off. The options window remembers where you put it. A one-time line on first login says what RangeShade does.
- Works with action bar addons whose buttons hold an action the standard way (Bartender, Dominos, ElvUI and similar), as well as the controller layout.

## 0.3.3

- **A minimap button:** click it for the options, drag it around the minimap's rim to move it, and hover it to see what's on. Hide it in the options or with `/rangeshade button`.

## 0.3.2

- **A ready ability keeps glowing until you use it,** in case you missed the flash: a soft, slow pulse over the button. It pauses for the moment of the global cooldown after each cast (the ability can't be used then anyway) and comes straight back; it stops when you use that ability or the fight ends. Switch it off with `/rangeshade glow` or in the options.

## 0.3.1

- **Works on the controller layout's buttons too.** RangeShade used to look only at the standard action bars by name, so the round buttons of the game's controller layout (and other bar addons' buttons) were neither shaded nor flashed. It now finds any button that holds an action.
- `/rangeshade find` says how many buttons it is watching; `/rangeshade flash test` flashes every button on screen at once so you can see the flash; `/rangeshade debug` now also counts cooldowns seen.

## 0.3.0

- **Flashes a button when its ability is ready again:** when an ability comes off cooldown, its button gives two quick bright pulses, so you see it's ready without watching the swirl. In fights only by default; switch it to always or off in the options or with `/rangeshade flash`.
- The short global cooldown every spell shares never flashes, only real cooldowns (two seconds or more). This works even where the game hides cooldown lengths from addons in a fight: RangeShade times the swirl itself.
- Pairs well with the game's own "Show Numbers for Cooldowns" (Options > Action Bars), which counts the seconds down on the swirl.

## 0.2.4

- **Controller:** when a fight starts, B goes straight back to its usual job, even with a RangeShade window open (it used to stay on closing the window until the fight ended). It closes the window again once the fight is over.

## 0.2.3

- **Controller:** the B button now closes RangeShade's window, like the X and Escape. While one is open, B closes it; once it is closed, B does whatever you have it set to again.

## 0.2.2

- First release on CurseForge. No changes to how the addon works.

## 0.2.1

- Fixed an error on every check ("bad argument #2 to IsHarmfulAction") that 0.2.0 raised in game and that stopped all shading.
- If the melee check ever hits a problem again, it switches itself off with one message; ordinary range shading carries on.

## 0.2.0

- Melee abilities are now shaded too, using a separate distance check, because the game reports them as in range at any distance. Can be turned off.
- `/rangeshade debug` lists what the game reports for each button.

## 0.1.0

- First version: shades action buttons red while their action cannot reach the target.
